objective: Log in to Dropbox with the 'dropbox' credential via the agent_web SDK, upload a short text file to your Dropbox account, verify it appears, and report the result.

nodes.description: Upload a short text file to Dropbox using the credentialed web SDK

success_criteria: A text file was uploaded to the Dropbox account
The upload was verified (or an explicit blocker such as a bot/CAPTCHA challenge is reported)
config.node_objective:
Use the agent_web SDK (import: from agent_web import web) with the credential reference 'dropbox' to log in to Dropbox and upload a short text file.

Steps:
1. Create /workspace/upload-to-dropbox/taskforge-hello.txt with the content 'Hello from TaskForge agent'.
2. Establish a credentialed session: s = web.session(credential="dropbox", impersonate="chrome"). The FIRST use of the 'dropbox' credential for https://www.dropbox.com triggers a human approval on the Approvals page - the call blocks until approved. If it raises CredentialDenied, stop and report that the credential was denied.
3. GET https://www.dropbox.com/home to confirm you are logged in (expected HTML status 200 and an authenticated page).
4. Upload the file using the Dropbox web upload endpoint POST https://www.dropbox.com/upload (multipart form field 'file', header 'Authorization' as the SPA provides; pass headers you observe on the upload request) with the same session. If Dropbox returns a reCAPTCHA/fingerprint challenge or an error page instead of a successful upload, STOP and report the blocker verbatim - do NOT retry in a loop and do NOT claim success.
5. Verify the upload: list the account root (GET https://www.dropbox.com/home or the upload/listing API) and confirm 'taskforge-hello.txt' is present.
6. Write /workspace/upload-to-dropbox/upload_result.json with {file: 'taskforge-hello.txt', uploaded: true/false, verified: true/false, notes: '<what actually happened>'}. Only set uploaded/verified true when you have real evidence.

Rules: never print or try to read the credential's password; never fabricate an upload; if you hit a bot challenge, 2FA, or denial, report exactly that.
